specimens.title: ThemedImage
specimens.topicHint: Any single theme, topic, or subject — one unique image out.
flaws: Seeded randomness (era, medium, palette) makes exact reruns unreproducible by design
The verify asserts are named, not defined — enforcement is the model's word

specimens.title: Anglish Poster (Calque Converter)
specimens.topicHint: A short phrase, slogan, or poster text to rebuild from Germanic roots.
flaws: No prompt text exists — the specimen is a single worked example, so conversion rules must be inferred from it
The example cheats on its own rule: 'MYSTERY-ONES' keeps a Greek/Latin loan
'UNWAVED' has no clear Old English root; 'WAKE OUTWARD' for 'watch out' is a stretch

specimens.title: Flocked Origami Sculpture
specimens.topicHint: Subjects with iconic silhouettes (the original brief used four historic battles).
flaws: Subject-type mismatch: section A assumes an iconic silhouette, but events like battles are not objects — the model must invent a vignette
The origami zone mask (wings, armor, hair, leaves, architecture) is generic boilerplate, never fitted to the subject
Header says 2x2 grid while the spec says 'Output: 1 image' — the grid/run relationship is never stated

specimens.title: Infographic Diorama
specimens.topicHint: A subject with a defining artifact silhouette, viewed across eras (original brief: toys by decade).
flaws: No verification block — floating leader lines pointing at nothing go ungated
Fixed 'numbered bullet points (1-12)' regardless of subject invites invented details
Header says 2x2 grid but the class renders one diorama; the era × topic matrix is never stated
Provenance note, Nov 4, 2026: the Timewave Zero infographic gadgetify posted as the Figma Cute Parody Poster's example image was actually produced by this prompt

specimens.title: Noir Storybook Poster
specimens.topicHint: One subject with a strong archetype — a detective, child, musician, dancer, animal, messenger.
flaws: Aspect contradiction: header says 16:9, Camera & Finish says 4:5 or 2:3
Typo in the specimen: SILHOUETTES resolves from '$ SUJECT' (kept verbatim)
The ∇P / ∇×P / ∇·F field math is theatrical — no model computes it; it works only as a composition cue

specimens.title: Personified Collage Poster
specimens.topicHint: Any topic that can be embodied as a mascot — a place, era, product, day, or event.
flaws: No verify step: title legibility, mascot share (55–70%), and the built-in-not-pasted-on rule are never checked
Composition is hardcoded portrait while format is a variable — setting 16:9 makes the two fight
Palette and mood resolve from single unconstrained infer_* calls

specimens.title: Semantic History Sculpture (Adaptive Timeline Artifact)
specimens.topicHint: Any subject with a history — an art, science, craft, technology, or industry.
flaws: The parents and mutations dicts are dead code: generate() never calls them; their contents leak only as paraphrase
No verify step — milestone recognizability, label legibility, and the no-generic-timeline rule are unchecked
Runs show garbled micro-type (duplicated and misspelled milestone labels)

specimens.title: Long-Exposure Integral Engine
specimens.topicHint: A scene with a still anchor and moving elements, plus one exposure duration T (e.g. 30 seconds).
flaws: No input slot in the specimen: scene and duration T must be supplied from outside
No render/execute step — the frame equation is the whole prompt
Transcribed from a screenshot: the formula's bracket layout and clip scope were reconstructed, not copied

specimens.title: Physics → Furniture Gallery
specimens.topicHint: Abstract concepts to analyze as furniture (original brief: famous physics concepts).
flaws: Rules key on undeclared attributes (Rigid, Reflective, Mechanical) that the ANALYZE step never declares
Partial coverage, no fallback: 5 rules against 48 declared combinations — most analyses match nothing
No conflict resolution when antecedents overlap, and several enum values (Sticky, Warm, Medium, Low) are dead

specimens.title: History Diorama (Typographic Terrain Plate)
specimens.topicHint: Historical events, each with a name, date, subtitle, and four chronological phases.
flaws: Triple ratio conflict: outer 16:9 grid vs template ratio='3:2' vs what a 2x2 split actually yields
Five unbound variables (PHASES, EVENT_TOKEN, SET_PIECES, CROWD_GRAMMAR, ATMOSPHERE); PHASES is load-bearing and nothing instructs the model to derive it
No verify or anti-fabrication rule — for history, the dates are the content and nothing audits them

specimens.title: Semantic Illustrated Wordmark Compiler
specimens.topicHint: A word or phrase and its topic, to compile into an illustrated vector logo.
flaws: No verify step at all — spelling, readability, and whether the promised letter transformations happened go unaudited
Pure inference with no floor: HARD_CODING = False and zero worked examples; the author reports 5 runs giving 5 very different results
Layout lives only in the outer run instruction; which text/topic pairs fill the cells is never declared

specimens.title: Sketchbook Biography Doodle Map
specimens.topicHint: A subject with a life or story to map — a person, film, place, invention, or founder.
flaws: The Oct 19 style-block restyle dropped the Oct 12 class version's verify() asserts (S1–S5) — more specification, less audit
SUBJECT is never bound in the Oct 19 version; subject, grid, and count arrive only via the run instruction
Runs show duplicated labels and labels leaking across grid cells

specimens.title: Totem Glyph Field
specimens.topicHint: Any topic with a motif language — a field of study, place, craft, or creature world.
flaws: The input was written broken ('$ TOPIC', with a space) and never assigned anywhere in the specimen
Stateless iteration: no registry of placed glyphs, so the exactly-26 A–Z guarantee is unenforceable by construction (both test runs failed grid_check)
Unbounded regeneration: 'IF ANY check fails → regenerate' states no retry limit and no keep-best fallback

specimens.title: Figma Cute Parody Poster
specimens.topicHint: A pop culture icon — a famous object, character, vehicle, or franchise symbol.
flaws: AI_INFER() is invoked four times, never defined, and carries all the creative content; the tree constrains layout and style only
Pseudo-Figma, not Figma: 'fill: # F5F5DC' has a space in the hex; components don't take children string arrays — costume notation
No canvas size or aspect ratio anywhere — output shape is a coin flip; no accuracy check or asserts
Example mismatch resolved Nov 4, 2026: the Timewave Zero infographic gadgetify posted as this prompt's example was actually produced by his Infographic Diorama prompt, not this one

specimens.title: Dual-Synthesis Poster Engine
specimens.topicHint: Any subject that can carry a poster — a neighborhood, person, event, product, or place.
flaws: Unseeded 'randomly select' in the original delegates the core creative act to the renderer, which drifts to safe favorites (the spinner rolls real dice instead)
Phase 1 only — no Phase 2: no title, typography, hierarchy, or finish spec; no asserts
Fusion has no arbiter or weights; when the two movements fight, the first rendered tends to dominate

specimens.title: Honest Caricature Laws
specimens.topicHint: A real situation with a clear power holder — a named person, decision, or headline to satirize or audit.
flaws: It is a conscience, not an engine: no render directive, no output format, no subject binding — it can only grade an image, not produce one
Circularity: P is 'readable directly from the staging', but staging is the only instrument supplied for measuring P
OVERDETERMINATION assumes the three P estimates agree and gives no tiebreaker when they don't
